statement: The vendored src/coordination/vendor/lock-policy.js#classifyClaimPair control-flow has a dead branch: the work-reservation-overlap advisory (line ~327) is unreachable for two exact-file claims sharing a path, because the earlier same-path+same-project+same-worktree check (line 302) always fires write-lock-conflict first regardless of lockKind, and the same-branch+different-worktree check (line 317) covers the remaining same-branch case. The workpack's own acceptance fixture ('two workReservation claims on same-branch overlapping path -> advisory only') describes behavior the vendored JS cannot actually produce for same-path claims.
why: A byte-for-byte Rust port that reproduces vendored precedence exactly will inherit this same reachability gap rather than the workpack's described behavior; a port that 'fixes' it silently diverges from the JS oracle used for cross-impl parity.
howToApply: When porting lock-policy.js precedence-ordered classifiers, verify workpack acceptance fixtures against the ACTUAL vendored control flow line-by-line before writing the fixture; if the fixture describes unreachable behavior, keep vendored parity and flag the gap rather than inventing new behavior to satisfy the fixture text.

statement: The live ocentra-enforcer coordination MCP tool (mcp__ocentra-enforcer__ocentra_enforcer_coordination_claim) still rejects glob/directory owns-set entries with 'claim paths must be exact files, not folders or globs' (L13 finding), confirmed live on this exact build on 2026-07-04 — the .mjs server has NOT yet been patched even though this Rust port's own api::normalize_owns_paths/claim_all fixes the same defect.
why: L13 was recorded as a finding but the running coordination server callers actually use today is unpatched; workers must keep manually enumerating+splitting claims until the arc-21/x03 cutover replaces the .mjs server with this crate's binary.
howToApply: Until the MCP coordination server is swapped to the Rust port, every worker must enumerate exact files and split into <=10-file claims per L13's original mitigation — do not assume the fix is live just because the Rust crate now has it.

evidence.ref: live coordination_claim call rejecting crates/enforcer-coordination/** during this session

statement: The live coordination_mail 'send' action ignores an explicit lane parameter and defaults sender identity to whatever lane last had default-identity resolution server-side (observed: passing lane='arc-16' to mail send still wrote lane='orchestrator-wiretest' on the event); the correct parameter to control sender lane on mail send is 'from', not 'lane'.
why: A worker following the protocol's literal 'lane' parameter name for mail send silently mails under the wrong identity, corrupting the presence/mail picture the orchestrator relies on for L4's started/progress/done lifecycle.
howToApply: When sending coordination mail as a specific lane, pass 'from': '<lane>' explicitly; do not rely on 'lane' alone for mail send (it appears to only affect claim/release actions, not message identity). Verify via inbox read-back after sending.

evidence.ref: coordination_mail send with lane=arc-16 produced writer node_de7774b31f384128b8f0e381fa35c8ae.orchestrator-wiretest; corrected by passing from=arc-16

statement: The live coordination hub's event context still resolves worktreeRoot/branch/cwd from the SERVER's own process cwd (observed: context.worktreeRoot=C:\Projects\enforcer-rust, branch=rust-build on a mail sent from worktree C:\Projects\ocentra-enforcer\.claude\worktrees\agent-a4dc67cd4bc20fccb on branch lane/arc-16) even though claim events DO correctly reflect caller-supplied worktreeRoot/branch when those params are passed explicitly. L2 is fixed for claim/release (caller params honored) but NOT fixed for mail/message events on the live .mjs server.
why: L2's fix is asymmetric across the live server's tool surface: claim/release honor caller identity, message/mail do not yet accept or use equivalent caller-context params, so mail's presence trail is still server-cwd-biased.
howToApply: Do not trust mail-event context.worktreeRoot/branch fields for cross-lane presence auditing until mail/message tools accept the same explicit caller-context params claim/release do; treat mail context as informational-only from the SENDING agent's own self-report in the mail body, not the event envelope.

evidence.ref: coordination_mail send event seq 3, context.worktreeRoot/branch/cwd all point at C:\Projects\enforcer-rust / rust-build despite caller running in a different worktree/branch

statement: This workspace's clippy proof convention (confirmed from proof/cargo/arc-18.txt and proof/cargo/arc-25.txt) runs 'cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings', which is STRICTER than the bare [workspace.lints.clippy] deny-list in Cargo.toml (only ~15 lints denied) — it also fails on any default-warn lint (too_many_arguments, derivable_impls, etc.), not just the explicitly denied ones.
why: A worker who only checks 'plain cargo clippy exits clean' (matching the workspace Cargo.toml deny-list) can still fail the real proof gate, which additionally requires zero default-warn-level lints across the whole crate.
howToApply: Always generate the proof artifact with 'cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings', not bare 'cargo clippy', and fix every resulting error (not just workspace-denied ones) before declaring the crate proof-green.

evidence.ref: proof/cargo/arc-18.txt line 126; proof/cargo/arc-16.txt (this pack) after fixing too_many_arguments via ClaimRequestArgs/AppendEventArgs param structs
